samples.summary: `templates publish` prints the listing response verbatim, including `previewToken` — a non-expiring anonymous read capability for the document — onto stdout
samples.evidence: `output(res.data, fmt)` (packages/cli/src/commands/templates.ts:162) relays the server payload untouched, and `output()`/`format()` do no redaction (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:86). `POST /documents/:id/template` returns a full `TemplateListingView`, whose `previewToken` is the `viewer` share-link token (`toView`, packages/backend/src/template/template.service.ts:1314) — the backend itself calls a page of these "a page of non-expiring read capabilities" (template.service.ts:1037) and deliberately strips it from collections. The new schema entry advertises it as part of the publish response (packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:1445), so agents are told to expect it. Vector: any capture of the command's stdout — an agent transcript, a CI job log, `wafflebase templates publish doc > out.json` in a repo — hands a reader anonymous read access to the published document's live content, with no expiry and no revocation other than unpublishing. Note the repo already treats stdout as a capture surface: `printDryRunUrl` strips URL userinfo precisely because "it goes to *stdout*, which is what an agent records" (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:40-45). Unlike `api-keys create`, where the secret is the point, the CLI never needs `previewToken`.

samples.summary: `templates.publish` is annotated `safety: 'write'` and its description never says a first publish mints a non-expiring anonymous viewer share link (default tier `unlisted`), so an agent treats an exposure-widening action as an ordinary content write
samples.evidence: registry.ts:1433-1446 declares `safety: 'write'` with a description about upsert semantics only; `--visibility` is documented as "unlisted or workspace" with default "unlisted on a first publish". What actually happens server-side is that `publish()` mints a `viewer` share link through `ShareLinkService.create(documentId, 'viewer', userId, null)` with no expiry (packages/backend/src/template/template.service.ts:373-375) and the `unlisted` tier returns `true` unconditionally from `isVisibleTo` (template.service.ts:1200) — i.e. anyone holding the listing UUID can read the document. docs/design/cli.md's safety table defines `destructive` as "Deletes data irreversibly → agent must ask for user confirmation" and has no level for "widens who can read this", and no `--yes`/confirmation exists on this command (the only confirmations in the CLI are the `--replace` ones in docs/slides/notes import). Vector: an agent auto-approving `write` operations publishes a workspace document and, by default, creates an anonymously readable link to it; the schema output it reads to decide gives it no signal. Searched the registry for any existing sharing command or exposure annotation and found none — `templates.publish` is the CLI's first such command, so the taxonomy gap is newly load-bearing here.

samples.summary: `templateBrowseParams` silently drops empty-string filters, so `--tag ""` / `--query ""` return the whole unfiltered gallery instead of the backend's deliberate 400
samples.evidence: `if (value !== undefined && value !== '') params.set(key, value)` (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:133) removes the filter client-side. The backend refuses the same input on purpose: `BrowseTemplatesDto.tag` carries `@Length(1, …)` plus `@Matches(/\S/)` with the comment that a value normalizing to nothing "would be dropped from the `where` clause — so `?tag=%20%20` would silently return the whole unfiltered gallery instead of the empty result the caller asked for. Refused here rather than repaired downstream" (packages/backend/src/template/template.dto.ts:166-179); `q` has `@Length(1,200)` and `@IsOptional()` does not skip `''`. So a caller (or a script interpolating an empty variable) that asks for a narrowed listing gets the full one with a 200 exit instead of a 400 — the exact silent-widening the DTO was hardened against, reintroduced one layer up, and also visible in the `--dry-run` preview as a URL with no filter. Disclosure stays inside the caller's authorized scope (public gallery, or a workspace `assertMember` passes), which is why this is minor rather than an authz break; the analogous empty-workspace case does fail closed (server 400 'workspaceId is required when scope is "workspace"'). Partly overlaps the correctness lens.
